title: Autonomous Ops Gateway: event-driven task orchestration for support flows
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Build an Autonomous Ops Gateway (AOG) that translates alerts, support requests, and incident signals into executable, auditable task graphs without thinking in ad-hoc scripts. The gateway should accept event inputs (webhooks, pubsub, PagerDuty, Slack), evaluate policy and SLO guardrails, synthesize a minimal set of actions, and execute through pluggable connectors (K8s operator API, SSH-less run actions, cloud SDKs, internal secrets vault) while producing deterministic audit trails and dry-run simulations. Goal: reduce mean time to resolution for common support patterns, remove maintenance burden of bespoke runbooks, and enable on-call safe automation with RBAC and approval gates. Scope: MVP covers three canonical flows (service restart + cache purge, roll-forward deploy, and user data export for compliance), connector SDK, policy engine with dry-run, audit log schema, and a console UI for simulation and approvals. Non-goals: replacing full incident commander workflows or advanced playbook authoring in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway ingests events from at least PagerDuty and Slack and maps them to a task template
Dry-run simulation returns deterministic action list with estimated latency and cost
Connectors execute actions without shell access (API-based) for K8s, GCP, and internal vault
Audit log entries created in structured JSON for every decision and action with trace IDs
RBAC gating and single-step human approval implemented for high-risk templates
E2E test harness exercises the three canonical flows with synthetic incidents
updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial scoping doc linked in Confluence. Identified three canonical flows for MVP.

2025-02-18: Architecture brainstorm with infra and security. Decided on event-to-DAG model vs. linear script model — chose DAG for parallelizable reduce time-to-fix. Trade-off: slightly more complex runtime state management.
2025-02-22: Prototype of connector SDK completed (internal repo link: github.com/redwood/aog-connector-proto PR #48). Prototype uses gRPC control channel and JWT-based connector auth.
2025-02-25: Security review kickoff. Security requested explicit KMS-wrapped secrets in transit + audit retention policy. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-27: Decision: default actions run in 'no-privilege' sandbox with token-scoped ephemeral creds. Rationale: minimize blast radius and enable least-privilege by default.
2025-03-02: Implemented dry-run engine and console simulation UI mockups. UX feedback from SRE shows desire for step-level explainability. TODO: add 'why' metadata to action decisions.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: enable for SREs in staging with logs-only mode (no actions) for 2 weeks
2) Beta: enable action execution for low-risk templates (read-only, cache purge) behind approval gate for a single service team
3) Gradual ramp to prod: expand approved templates and services over 4 weeks with canary audit verification
4) Post-rollout: run a table-top incident drill and collect MTTR/false-positive metrics
